thread.title: Tech Shares Likely To Weigh On Taiwan Stock Market

title: Tech Shares Likely To Weigh On Taiwan Stock Market
text:
(RTTNews) - The Taiwan stock market inched barely higher again on Monday, one session after it had ended the two-day winning streak in which it had advanced more than 120 points or 1.2 percent. The Taiwan Stock Exchange remains just above the 9,830-point plateau although it figures to head south again on Tuesday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets is soft, with weakness expected among the technology stocks and oil companies. The European and U.S. markets were down and the Asian bourse are expected to follow suit.
The TSE finished barely higher on Monday following gains from the cement stocks and mixed performances from the technology companies and financial shares.
For the day, the index gained 1.20 points or 0.01 percent to finish at 9,831.21 after trading between 9,764.46 and 9,875.84 on turnover of 90.41 billion Taiwan dollars.
Among the actives, Cathay Financial and Fubon Financial both lost 0.39 percent, while CTBC Financial dipped 0.24 percent, Mega Financial collected 0.19 percent, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company gained 0.22 percent, United Microelectronics Corporation perked 0.94 percent, Hon Hai Precision added 0.13 percent, Largan Precision skidded 0.97 percent, AU Optronics gathered 1.23 percent, Acer plunged 4.93 percent, AsusTek Computer shed 0.65 percent, Chunghwa Telecom fell 0.47 percent, Taiwan Cement spiked 2.01 percent, Asia Cement advanced 1.97 percent and Formosa Plastic and Formosa Chemical were unchanged.
The lead from Wall Street is broadly negative as stocks moved sharply lower on Monday, extending losses from the previous session.
The Dow plunged 602.12 points or 2.32 percent to 25,387.18, while the NASDAQ dropped 206.03 points or 2.78 percent to 7,200.87 and the S&P fell 54.79 points or 1.97 percent to 2,726.22.
A sharp decline by shares of Apple (AAPL) and General Electric (GE) weighed on the markets, while concerns about the outlook for global economic growth and a continued increase in interest rates also contributed to the sell-off.
Light trading activity may have exaggerated the downward move, however, as government offices, the bond markets, and most banks were closed in observance of Veterans Day.
Crude oil shook off early gains on Monday to end lower for the 11th straight session on oversupply concerns. Crude oil futures for December, which rose to $61.28 earlier in the session, settled lower by $0.26 or 0.4 percent at $59.93 a barrel, the lowest settlement since February.
